text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Tuesday:
- Switzerland and the European Union signed a bilateral customs deal which commits both parties to cooperate in customs matters such as fraud.
- Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) plans to take over Belgian shoe repair chain Mister Minit. UBS reported that it will prepare the company to be listed on the stock exchange in London or Amsterdam.

- Swiss high-tech group Esec said it still aims to break the one billion Swiss franc sales barrier by the year 2000 despite disapointing figures in 1996/97. Net profits dropped by 58 percent to 11 million francs.

- The decision to abolish an inheritance tax in the canton of St Gallen has immediate effects in the other regions. Zurich, Thurgau, and Appenzell will start discussions to get rid of the tax as well.
- The Swiss government will send special troops to the border between Switzerland and Italy in order to hinder Albanian refugees from entering Switzerland.
- Swiss unemployment insurance need an extra 3.4 billion Swiss francs in credits to guarantee its services. A tax raise is not expected.
- The lower house of parliament voted to change continuing education policies as 16 to 19 year olds face severe problems in finding jobs as trainees.
